there is a BASE_SPECIAL (not sure of the name...) for this
I am not sure that I understand. A special value for 0xffff in packet-someip-sd.c? I am not aware of that.

`BASE_SPECIAL_VALS` is for when a value string is used only for special values, but for values not found, nothing is added instead of putting "Unknown".

So if you did

```c
static const value_string sd_eventgroupid[] = {
    {0xFFFF,    "ANY"},
    {0, NULL}
};
...
        { &hf_someip_sd_entry_eventgroupid,
            { "Eventgroup ID", "someipsd.entry.eventgroupid",
            FT_UINT16, BASE_HEX|BASE_SPECIAL_VALS, VALS(sd_eventgroup_id), 0x0, NULL, HFILL }},
```

It will appear in the tree like

```
Eventgroup ID: ANY (0xFFFF)
```

for those and just

```
Eventgroup ID: 0x1234
```

for values not in the value_string.

changed this line in [version 4 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/13947/diffs?diff_id=890089408&start_sha=b5ac7754cbd0122a5b5d39dc4206d44477744e5b#d6a779c0e987a60ff5919e3cab8f6038353c33da_710_721)
Prepared a change as requested. Still think it looks quite inconsistent but so you can try it out.

I know the value_strings but I have chosen not to use them here since for SOME/IP a lot of the names for values can be configured. e.g., Service-ID, Method-ID, Eventgroup-ID, Client-ID, etc.

If we use a value string it looks like this:
- Eventgroup ID: 0x1111
- Eventgroup ID: 0x2222 (name-if-configured)
- Eventgroup ID: ANY (0xffff)

I prefer to NOT have such inconsistent output with sometimes value first and sometimes name first. Because of that I prefer to use proto_item_append_text.

The alternative would be to rewrite the Wireshark handling of value_strings and allow to configure what is first!?
but with proto_item_append_txt, it isn ot possible to search with ....eventgroup_id = ANY

Yes that is right but until now you could only search like this:
> someipsd.entry.eventgroupid == 0xffff
So still an improvement. :upside_down: 

I change the code and tried:
> someipsd.entry.eventgroupid == ANY

This seems to not fully work since the filter field turns yellow, which seems to warn me not to filter like that. Is this expected? Am I doing something wrong?

And again, this change would make it really look inconsistent. :disappointed:

Tried some more. I already had a field for configured names: someipsd.entry.eventgroupname, which works for filtering. The issue I see is that the eventgroupname has to be resolved in context of the serviceid. If you need to use someipsd.entry.eventgroupname for all but the ANY value, this might confuse the user a lot, don't you think?
Prepared a change as requested. Still think it looks quite inconsistent but so you can try it out.
